title: On-Prem & VPC Tiered Entitlement, Migration Credits, and Security Playbook
creator: Priya Shah
description: Create a repeatable playbook and experiment plan for packaging Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem) that balances license fee mathematics, support tiers, upgrade cadence, and responses to typical enterprise security questionnaires. Deliverables: 1) a 3-tier entitlement matrix (Core, Enterprise, Elite) with license fee guidance and unit economics examples; 2) migration credit rules and practical examples for customers moving from Hosted to Private; 3) recommended support tiers (Standard, Priority, Dedicated SA) with SLAs and escalation flow; 4) upgrade/patch cadence options and contract language for EOL/upgrade windows; 5) canonical answers and evidence artifacts for common security questionnaire items; 6) negotiation playbook including concession guardrails, auto-addons, and pilot discounts. This ticket coordinates PM, Legal, Security, Sales Engineering, and Product to produce a single-page playbook + detailed appendix for legal and SE use.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing matrix with three named bundles and example customer scenarios showing list price, effective price after migration credit, and per-token economics
Contract clause templates for upgrade cadence (annual major, quarterly patch windows) and a standard EOL notice period (12 months) approved by Legal
Migration credit policy documented: eligibility, credit calculation examples, and how credits apply to first 12 months of committed spend
Security questionnaire canonical answers for the top 25 enterprise questions with at least 3 attached evidence artifacts (SOC/ISO summary, network diagram, KMS integration guide)
Pilot checklist and success metrics (time to onboard, baseline latency, cost delta, security attestation) and an experiment plan for 5 pilot customers
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Decided to test three bundles instead of four to reduce complexity for Sales; tiers are Core/Enterprise/Elite with optional add-on modules for observability and higher retention windows
2026-03-12: Agreed migration credit should be a capped percentage of first-year committed spend (recommended 20%) rather than a per-instance rebate to avoid gaming
2026-03-13: Legal prefers 'upgrade windows' language over hard auto-upgrade commitments; opted for customer-selectable cadence with default annual major + quarterly security patches
2026-03-14: Security sign-off on canonical questionnaire answers pending final proof artifacts; plan to bundle SOC2 summary and KMS architecture diagram in appendix
